notes.summary: The few cryptographic primitives a network client needs around its transport, in `@dream/bytes` behind `bytes-crypto`: bytes from the operating system's CSPRNG, HMAC with constant-time verification, and RS256 signatures, all through the ring that `tls` already builds.
added: `bytes.random(count)`: up to 65536 bytes from the operating system's CSPRNG per call, for keys, nonces and WebSocket masks, where `math.random` is none of those.

`bytes.hmac(data, key, algorithm)` with `sha1`, `sha256`, `sha384` or `sha512`, the raw tag, and `bytes.hmacVerify(data, key, algorithm, tag)`, which compares in constant time, for checking a webhook's signature without timing what matched. Both match the RFC 2202 and RFC 4231 vectors.

`bytes.rsaSign(data, privateKey, algorithm)`: the raw PKCS#1 v1.5 RSA signature, RS256, RS384 or RS512 as JSON Web Tokens name them, from a key of at least 2048 bits in PKCS#8 or PKCS#1, PEM or DER, as services issue keys for signing tokens. The signature is byte for byte OpenSSL's. An encrypted key, an EC key or anything else is refused with a message that never quotes the key, and the decoded key bytes are zeroed when the call returns.
notes.migration:
Nothing to change. Take 2.4.0 in place of 2.3.0.

`bytes-crypto` is opt-in and adds no new dependency to a build that already has `tls`: it is ring, which `tls` builds, and zeroize. Turned on without `tls`, it builds ring's C and assembly with clang, as `tls` does.

There are no ciphers, no key generation and no key storage, and none are planned: a key arrives as bytes the caller holds and leaves with the call.

notes.summary: MP3, Vorbis and Opus decoding with `@dream/audio`; Luau 0.744, with its native code fixes and faster `table.find` and `table.create`; register reuse, so the 200-local limit counts only the locals still live; and analysis that types comprehensions and slices the way the loops they stand for are typed.
added: `@dream/audio` (feature `audio`): MP3 (and MPEG layers I and II) through nanomp3, Ogg Vorbis through lewton, and Ogg Opus through libopus built from the `opus` submodule, into interleaved `f32` buffers. Lengths are exact after gapless trimming, seeks land on the frame asked for (Opus after a 400 ms pre-roll), `audio.decode` caps its output at `maxSize`, and a damaged stream fails the read where it breaks. Decoding reads only the bytes it is given: no file, no device, no capability.

Named option records for the `@dream/bytes` calls a script reaches through `pcall`: `dream_bytes_RegexOptions` for `regex`, `dream_bytes_DecompressOptions` for `inflate` and `lzmaDecompress`, and `dream_bytes_DecompressLimit` for the LZ4 and zstd decoders. An options literal passed through `pcall` gets no expected type, so a caller annotates a local with the name instead of spelling the record out.
changed: Luau 0.744, from 0.742. The C API is unchanged; the fourteen flags 0.743 and 0.744 graduated leave the policy with their behaviour kept.

`table.find` scans the array part directly when the value has no `__eq`, and `table.create` and `table.clear` compile to fastcalls. In one release build: `table.find` over eight elements 34 to 22 ns for a hit and 41 to 23 ns for a miss, over a thousand 2.99 to 0.52 µs; `table.create(8)` 64 to 51 ns, `table.create(64, 0)` 149 to 128 ns; clearing eight entries about 11 to 7 ns.

Luau's register reuse is on: once a local's last read has run, its register goes to the next local, so a function needs fewer stack slots and the 200-local limit counts only the locals still live. A chain of a thousand short-lived locals compiles where it was `Out of local registers`. Dialect code gets the same, with the lowering keeping each local's register until its last read in the code that runs.

From optimisation level 1, a debugger stopped after a local's last read no longer finds that local, because its register has gone to another. Compile at optimisation level 0 to keep every local in scope until its block ends.

A comprehension that is the whole initializer of an annotated local (`local items: T = [...]`), or the whole value of a `return` in a function declaring one result type, has each projection checked against `T`'s element type, as the loop it stands for would. `local pairs: { [string | number]: Value } = [for i in range(1, n) => { i, 'a' }]` is accepted where Luau's invariant table indexers refused the `{ { number | string } }` the projection inferred alone, and a misspelled record field is still an error. Compiled code is unchanged.
fixed: Luau 0.744's native code fixes: dead store elimination kept a tag store whose load had been overwritten, `INVOKE_FASTPCALL` now invalidates the safe-environment assumption, a VM exit's register restores are planned per exit (a crash Luau's fuzzer found), a libunwind unwinder registers each FDE on its own as Intel macOS needs, and on A64 `bit32.lrotate` no longer overwrites an operand it still reads and a function with more than 256 constants no longer crashes reloading one.

A slice that is the whole source of a `for ... in` header, `for _, v in values[1:n] do`, type checks as the table it is. The new solver read it against the iterator protocol and reported it as the wrong type.
notes.migration:
Nothing to change for most hosts. Take 2.3.0 in place of 2.2.0.

A debugger that shows every local, or a test that reads a local after its last use, compiles at `optimization_level: 0`. The defaults (level 2) now free a dead local's register.

`@dream/audio` is opt-in, behind the `audio` feature. A binary built with it ships libopus and must reproduce its BSD 3-Clause notice, `opus/COPYING`.

Scripts that spelled out `regex`'s options for a `pcall` can annotate with `dream_bytes_RegexOptions`, and comprehensions that cast each projection to their local's element type can drop the cast. A comprehension that reads a narrowed variable from outside its enclosing function still needs that value bound to a local first; the dialect page says why.
